clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old male presented with a 3-week history of red eye and a firm, oval, dark brown, vascular subconjunctival mass on the right eye measuring 7 × 6 × 3.2 mm, without intraocular extension on fundoscopy and gonioscopy. Ultrasound biomicroscopy revealed a subconjunctival mass with intact sclera except for temporal posterior shadowing suspicious of intraocular extension. Histopathological examination of the excisional biopsy showed large vascular channels lined by endothelial cells filled with red blood cells without malignancy, consistent with cavernous hemangioma. The patient had no recurrence after 6 months of follow-up.
